summary: Adversarial review of the Pesto anti-collision fixes diff (registry during processing, close release, seed, out-of-domain share auth, held switch)

confirmed.title: Closing Pesto can still leave a permanent 'Réservé par Pesto' AD account: the close cleanup misses AD reservations and releases that are still in flight
confirmed.scenario:
The close cleanup (Stop-PestoJoinADReservationAtClose, Pesto-Join.ps1:918-920) only looks at $script:JoinADReservation. Two in-flight cases slip through.
(1) Release in flight. The technician answers 'Non' at the join confirmation (Pesto-Join.ps1:596). Stop-PestoJoinADReservation sets $script:JoinADReservation=$null (line 903) and starts the async 'JoinADRelease<guid>' worker (line 906). That worker needs a runspace, a background-gate slot and an ActiveDirectory module import (several seconds). If the technician closes Pesto right away, the close cleanup sees $null and does nothing. Add_Closed then calls Stop-PestoAsyncOperation on every op (Pesto-Core.ps1:5196), which BeginStops the release before Remove-ADComputer runs.
(2) Reservation in flight. The window is closed while 'JoinADReserve' (line 868) is creating the account. Add_Closing does not block this op. New-ADComputer can finish while the result is discarded.
In both cases the computer account stays in AD with no expiry and blocks that number for every station, which is exactly what item 4 is meant to prevent. There is no other cleanup path for 'Réservé par Pesto' accounts.
confirmed.fix:
Track pending AD work at close.
- In Stop-PestoJoinADReservation, keep the reservation record (for example $script:JoinADReleasePending=$r) and clear it in the OnSuccess/OnError callbacks.
- In Stop-PestoJoinADReservationAtClose, if a release is still pending, run the same synchronous release, which is idempotent: it returns Gone or Kept when there is nothing to do.
- If the 'JoinADReserve' op is running, wait on its Async.AsyncWaitHandle within the same 8 s budget. Call EndInvoke, and if the result is State=Reserved, release that GUID synchronously.

verdict.evidence:
I tried to refute this and could not. Both in-flight paths are reachable, and nothing else ever cleans up an orphaned account. One limit: the whole feature is opt-in, because POLICY.ReserveNamesInAD defaults to $false (Pesto-Policy.ps1:8).

**Case 1: release still running at close.**
- The "Non" answer at Pesto-Join.ps1:596 calls Stop-PestoJoinADReservation.
- That function nulls $script:JoinADReservation (Pesto-Join.ps1:903) before it starts the async 'JoinADRelease<guid>' op (Pesto-Join.ps1:906).
- The same happens on code≠10/97/98 (Pesto-Join.ps1:645) and when the form is changed (Pesto-Join.ps1:944).
- The release is a non-mutation op. Its worker waits for a background-gate slot (Pesto-Async.ps1:211-216), dot-sources the AD loader and runs Import-PestoADModule, and only then calls Get-ADComputer/Remove-ADComputer (Pesto-Join.ps1:827-844). That is several seconds on PS 5.1.
- Add_Closing (Pesto-Core.ps1:5201-5211) blocks only $script:Running and QueueAction/DomainJoin/DirectAction/RecoveryAction (Pesto-Async.ps1:78-83). It stops only JoinCheck/JoinStatus, so the window closes.
- Add_Closed calls Stop-PestoJoinADReservationAtClose first (Pesto-Core.ps1:5185). It sees $null at Pesto-Join.ps1:918-919 and returns.
- The foreach at Pesto-Core.ps1:5196 then calls Stop-PestoAsyncOperation, which BeginStops the release (Pesto-Async.ps1:113-118). Then `Quit 0` → `exit` (Pesto-Core.ps1:5272, 1218) kills the process.
- If Remove-ADComputer has not run yet, the account stays. The UI has just told the technician "la réservation du nom dans l'AD est retirée" (Pesto-Join.ps1:597).

**Case 2: reservation still running at close.**
- 'JoinADReserve' (Pesto-Join.ps1:868) sets JoinBusy, but Add_Closing does not check JoinBusy or that op.
- $script:JoinADReservation is set only in the dispatcher callback (Pesto-Join.ps1:891), so AtClose sees $null.
- Add_Closed waits before it BeginStops anything: Stop-PestoAuditWriter Close(3000) (Pesto-Journal.ps1:205) and the up-to-3 s registry release in Stop-PestoSharedNameTimer (Pesto-Names.ps1:549). During that wait the worker keeps running and can reach New-ADComputer (Pesto-Join.ps1:849).
- BeginStop does not roll back an ADWS add that was already sent. The created account is never recorded.

**No other cleanup path.**
- A grep for "Réservé par Pesto" finds it only inside the reserve/release worker and the close function. Nothing sweeps orphaned accounts.
- After a restart, $script:JoinADReservation is empty, so New-PestoJoinPlanFromUI (Pesto-Join.ps1:317-318) does not treat the account as ours. The check sees the name as taken and moves on, so that number stays blocked for every station.

This is not a regression: before the diff, closing never released anything. But it is a concrete gap in the goal of item 4, and the timing windows are realistic: closing a few seconds after "Non" or during "Réservation du nom dans l'AD". My severity estimate is medium-low because the policy is opt-in.
verdict.adjusted_fix:
**1. Track releases in flight.**
- In Stop-PestoJoinADReservation, add the record to a pending list before starting the release, e.g. `$script:JoinADReleasePending[[string]$r.Guid]=$r`.
- Remove it in both the OnSuccess and OnError callbacks (pass the Guid in the CallbackContext).

**2. Extend Stop-PestoJoinADReservationAtClose so all close work shares one 8 s budget:**
- **Releases.** Gather $script:JoinADReservation plus every pending-release record. Release them in one synchronous worker call, or in sequence, using a stopwatch for the remaining time. Release is idempotent: it returns Gone, Kept or Released.
- **Reservation in flight.** If Test-PestoAsyncOperationRunning 'JoinADReserve', read the op from $script:PestoAsyncOperations; it is still there because AtClose runs first. Wait on `$op.Async.AsyncWaitHandle.WaitOne(remaining)`. On completion, call `@($op.PowerShell.EndInvoke($op.Async))|Select -Last 1`. If State -eq 'Reserved', release that Guid synchronously and mark the op Completed so the timer ignores it.
- **Log** any record not confirmed within the budget, as is done now.

**3. Simpler alternative for case 2.** In Add_Closing, refuse to close (`$e.Cancel=$true` plus a message) while 'JoinADReserve' or any 'JoinADRelease*' op is running. This matches how DomainJoin is treated and avoids both races without blocking the close path.

confirmed.title: A name that is only reserved in the shared registry is blacklisted for the whole session and logged as 'déjà utilisé dans l'AD'
confirmed.scenario:
The new pre-confirmation branches call Select-PestoJoinNextName (Pesto-Join.ps1:584-585) and Select-PestoDirectNextName (Pesto-Direct.ps1:310-311) for a name that another station holds only in the registry. That hold lasts 15 to 240 minutes and is released when the other Pesto closes.
Both Select functions add the name to $script:PestoTakenNames (Pesto-Join.ps1:469, Pesto-Direct.ps1:249). That set is documented as names found taken in AD, never proposed again for the session, and is only cleared in Initialize-PestoJoinUI. Both functions also log '<name> déjà utilisé dans l'AD' (Pesto-Join.ps1:477, Pesto-Direct.ps1:262).
Example: technician B abandons, or closes Pesto and releases the name. Station A will still never propose that number again in this session. With RandomNameChoice=0 ('premier numéro libre'), A permanently skips the lowest free number, and the Journal claims an AD conflict that never existed.
confirmed.fix:
Add a parameter such as -Transient to the Select-*NextName functions.
- For a registry hold, do not add the name to PestoTakenNames. Get-PestoJoinNameCandidates and Update-NameList already exclude names reserved by others for as long as the hold lasts.
- Log a registry-specific message instead of 'déjà utilisé dans l'AD'.

verdict.evidence:
I tried to refute this and could not. The finding holds.

Both new pre-confirmation branches send a name that is held only in the registry into the existing Select-*NextName functions:
- Join: Pesto-Join.ps1:582-585 calls Select-PestoJoinNextName with the Reason 'est réservé par un autre poste dans le registre partagé.'
- Direct: Pesto-Direct.ps1:308-311 does the same with Select-PestoDirectNextName.

Neither function checks why the name was rejected. Each adds it to the session blacklist without condition:
- Pesto-Join.ps1:468-469: `[void]$script:PestoTakenNames.Add($TakenName)`
- Pesto-Direct.ps1:248-249: the same call.

Both functions also log an AD conflict that never happened:
- Pesto-Join.ps1:477: `Add-LogLine "JONCTION : $TakenName déjà utilisé dans l'AD ; nom suivant proposé : $next."`
- Pesto-Direct.ps1:262: the same line for RENOMMAGE.

The on-screen text does carry the registry Reason. The Journal line and the message title 'Nom déjà pris' do not.

The blacklist lasts for the whole session:
- PestoTakenNames is reset only in Initialize-PestoJoinUI (Pesto-Join.ps1:768).
- That function is called once, at startup (Pesto-Core.ps1:5143).
- Name lists filter on it permanently: Get-PestoJoinNameCandidates (Pesto-Join.ps1:442) and Update-NameList (Pesto-Core.ps1:3109).
- Test-PestoNameReservedByOther (Pesto-Names.ps1:349-358) is time-bounded: it returns false once the hold expires or is no longer in SharedNameOthers. The blacklist entry stays after that.

Failure scenario: station B releases or abandons the name (closes Pesto, cancels, or the TTL expires). Station A still never proposes it again in that session. With RandomNameChoice=0 ('premier numéro libre'), A permanently skips the lowest free number, which hurts most in a long Direct (multi-PC) session. The Journal also records a false 'déjà utilisé dans l'AD'.

Impact is low. It causes a numbering gap and a misleading audit line. It does not cause a wrong join or rename.

Why the static tests and the benches would miss it: they check that A switches to the next name. They do not check that the held name becomes available again after B releases it, or the wording of the log line.
verdict.adjusted_fix:
1. Add a `[switch]$Transient` parameter to Select-PestoJoinNextName (Pesto-Join.ps1:462) and Select-PestoDirectNextName (Pesto-Direct.ps1:243).
2. When -Transient is set, skip `$script:PestoTakenNames.Add($TakenName)`. While the hold lasts, the name is still excluded by Test-PestoNameReservedByOther in Get-PestoJoinNameCandidates (Pesto-Join.ps1:444) and Update-NameList (Pesto-Core.ps1:3109).
3. If the hold expires between the test and Update-*, the same name comes back. The existing `$next -ieq $TakenName` guard then returns $false, and the caller continues normally with that name. This is acceptable because nobody holds it any more.
4. Build the Journal line from $Reason instead of the hard-coded AD text, for example `Add-LogLine "JONCTION : $TakenName $Reason Nom suivant proposé : $next." 'warn'`. Do the same for RENOMMAGE.
5. When transient, use a registry-specific title, for example 'Nom réservé par un autre poste : nom suivant proposé'.
6. Pass -Transient only from the two new registry branches (Pesto-Join.ps1:585 and Pesto-Direct.ps1:311). Leave the AD-taken callers unchanged: Pesto-Join.ps1:574/656/887 and Pesto-Direct.ps1:291/420.

confirmed.title: The registry worker checks the share root instead of the registry folder, and the credentialed SMB connection lasts for the whole logon session
confirmed.scenario:
The worker decides whether to connect with $Request.Credential based on [IO.Directory]::Exists('\\server\share') (lines 226-233), before checking the marker. Get-PestoCoordinationRoot does it the other way: it checks the marker first.
This breaks in-domain explicit-credential mode when the process token can read \\server\share\pesto (for example through bypass-traverse rights) but not the share root.
- Before this change: the registry worked.
- Now, if the logon session already has an SMB session to that server (home drive, mapped drive), New-PSDrive -Credential fails with 1219 (conflicting credentials). The catch then throws on every Snapshot, Reserve and Release, so the registry becomes permanently 'indisponible' on that station.
- If no session exists yet, the connection succeeds as the admin account.
In both cases, FileSystem New-PSDrive -Credential without -Persist creates a deviceless WNetAddConnection2 connection. That connection belongs to the logon session, not the process (contrary to the 'session réseau du processus' comments), and nothing ever removes it. Until logoff, every process of that user (Explorer, for example) reaches every share on that server with the AD admin identity.
confirmed.fix: In the worker, test [IO.File]::Exists($marker) or [IO.Directory]::Exists($root) first, as Get-PestoCoordinationRoot does. Only try the credentialed connect when that fails, and do not throw when New-PSDrive fails: fall through to the normal marker error. Record the connections you create and remove them at close (Remove-PSDrive, or WNetCancelConnection2 on the share in Stop-PestoSharedNameTimer). Fix the comments to say the connection is logon-session wide.

verdict.evidence:
I tried to refute this finding and could not. The code facts hold. The impact is narrower than the scenario says, so severity stays low.

**1) Wrong order of checks (confirmed).**
- In DEV/wad/Pesto-Names.ps1:226-233, the worker connects whenever `$Request.Credential` is non-null and `[IO.Directory]::Exists('\\srv\share')` is false. It checks the share root before it checks the marker at :234/:253.
- The old worker (HEAD) went straight to the marker.
- Get-PestoCoordinationRoot (Pesto-Policy.ps1:98-101) checks the marker first and calls Connect-PestoCoordinationShare only when the marker is unreadable.
- `$script:cred` is non-null in 'Explicit' mode in both cases, in-domain or not (Pesto-Authentication.ps1:68, :325-339).
- If New-PSDrive fails, the catch at :231 throws, so every Snapshot, Reserve and Release fails. 1219 is a known error in this code base (Pesto-Operations.ps1:602).
- **Limit:** the regression needs the process token to fail on the share root while it can still read root\pesto. On NTFS, FILE_READ_ATTRIBUTES on the root is usually granted implicitly through List on the parent folder of the share on the server. That ACL setup is uncommon but possible.

**2) Connection lifetime (confirmed).**
- FileSystemProvider.NewDrive with -Credential and no -Persist goes through MapNetworkDrive. That calls WNetAddConnection2 with no local name and CONNECT_NOPERSIST.
- This is a deviceless connection owned by the logon session (LUID), not by the process. It outlives the runspace and the process; only RemoveDrive or WNetCancelConnection2 removes it.
- Nothing ever removes it. A grep finds no Remove-PSDrive, WNetCancel or `net use /delete`. Stop-PestoSharedNameTimer (Pesto-Names.ps1:535-553) releases the reservations only.
- The drive is created in throwaway worker runspaces with -Scope Global, so no other runspace could even remove it by name.
- The comments at Pesto-Names.ps1:225 and Pesto-Policy.ps1:78-79 say "session réseau du processus", which is wrong.
- The same issue exists in Connect-PestoCoordinationShare (Pesto-Policy.ps1:86).

**3) Correction to the Explorer example.** Pesto always runs elevated (Pesto-Startup.ps1:32-42).
- With UAC split tokens, the connection lives in the elevated logon session. Explorer (filtered token) does not get it, unless EnableLinkedConnections is set.
- Every later elevated process of that user does get it until logoff. That includes a second Pesto started with another account: it then finds the share reachable and writes as the old account.
- Explorer does share it when Pesto runs under the built-in Administrator (no split token by default) or with UAC off. That is a realistic setup for an out-of-domain station being prepared.
- Domain join usually reboots, which ends the session. A Direct operation or a cancelled join leaves the connection to the server, authenticated as the AD admin, until logoff.
verdict.adjusted_fix:
1. In $script:PestoSharedNameWorker (Pesto-Names.ps1:226-233), copy the order used by Get-PestoCoordinationRoot. First try `[IO.File]::Exists($marker)` with the process token. Call New-PSDrive -Credential only if that fails and the root is a UNC path.
2. Do not throw when New-PSDrive fails (1219 or any other error). Keep the message and fall through to the normal marker check at :253, so a station that could already read the marker keeps working.
3. When the worker or Connect-PestoCoordinationShare actually creates a connection (the share was not reachable before), return the UNC path. Keep it in a script-level list on the UI side.
4. In Stop-PestoSharedNameTimer, after the release, cancel only the connections Pesto created. Use WNetCancelConnection2(unc, 0, false) through P/Invoke, or `net use \\srv\share /delete`. Remove-PSDrive will not work here, because the drive lives in a throwaway runspace.
5. Correct the comments at Pesto-Names.ps1:225 and Pesto-Policy.ps1:78-79. The connection is shared by the whole (elevated) logon session and outlives the process.

confirmed.title: Credentialed SMB connection to the registry server is never removed, so it outlives Pesto and is reused under the wrong account
confirmed.scenario:
Both Connect-PestoCoordinationShare (Pesto-Policy.ps1:86) and the registry worker (Pesto-Names.ps1:230) call New-PSDrive -Credential on a UNC root without -Persist. In Windows PowerShell 5.1 this makes a deviceless WNetAddConnection2 connection. Only Remove-PSDrive cancels that connection (FileSystemProvider.RemoveDrive -> WNetCancelConnection2), and nothing in DEV/wad ever calls Remove-PSDrive. Closing the runspace or exiting the process does not cancel it either. The connection belongs to the logon session, not to the process, so the comment 'session réseau du processus' is wrong. For an elevated admin token that means the linked elevated logon session, which lasts until logoff.

Concrete cases:
(a) On an out-of-domain staging PC logged on as a local admin, technician A opens Pesto with A's AD admin account, then cancels or closes without joining. Until logoff, any elevated process in that Windows session (admin PowerShell, Explorer started as admin, and so on) can reach \\fileserver\* as A. That includes other shares and admin shares on the same server, because the redirector keeps one credential per server per logon session. The same applies on a tiered technician workstation: the daily account is a local admin and the admin account is typed into Pesto.
(b) Technician B then starts Pesto in the same Windows session. [IO.Directory]::Exists($share) returns true through A's session, so no new connection is made. Registry entries and the coordination lock files (Enter-PestoCoordination) are written on the server under A's identity while the receipts say B.
(c) If A's session cannot read the share, New-PSDrive with B's credential fails with 1219. Get-PestoCoordinationRoot then throws, which blocks every mutation when CoordinationRequired is set, and the message does not include the 'nettoyer les sessions net use' guidance.
(d) If the share is on the server name used for the join (for example \\dc01.domaine\pesto$), NetJoinDomain's IPC$ connection with a different credential can fail with 1219. AddToDomain classifies any code other than 5/1314/1326 as 97 ('Jonction engagée, résultat non confirmé'), so the join locks as Uncertain.
confirmed.fix: Make one connection, owned by the main runspace (for example at login), and remember its share and drive. Cancel it with Remove-PSDrive or WNetCancelConnection2(share,0,true) in Add_Closed, on logout or credential change, and before opening a connection for another account. Workers should not open connections of their own; they should report that the share is unreachable. Before reusing an existing connection, check that its user is the current $script:cred.UserName (for example through Win32_NetworkConnection.UserName), and handle 1219 with an explicit message. Fix the comment that says the scope is per process.

verdict.evidence:
I could not refute the core claim. Two cases in the scenario are weaker than reported.

1. The diff adds both connections, and nothing removes them.
   - Pesto-Policy.ps1:86 (Connect-PestoCoordinationShare) and Pesto-Names.ps1:230 (the registry worker) both call `New-PSDrive -PSProvider FileSystem -Root \\srv\share -Credential ... -Scope Global` without `-Persist`.
   - In Windows PowerShell 5.1, FileSystemProvider.IsNetworkMappedDrive is true for a UNC root with a non-empty credential. NewDrive then calls MapNetworkDrive, which runs WNetAddConnection2 with LocalName=null and CONNECT_NOPERSIST. That makes a deviceless redirector connection.
   - A grep of DEV/wad finds no Remove-PSDrive, no WNetCancelConnection and no `net use /delete`. The only "1219" is a schtasks hint at Pesto-Operations.ps1:602.
   - WNet connections belong to the logon session, not the process. They last until they are cancelled or the user logs off; closing a runspace or exiting the process does not end them. The comments at Pesto-Policy.ps1:79 and Pesto-Names.ps1:225 ("session réseau du processus") are wrong.
   - Pesto runs elevated (Pesto-Authentication.ps1:360, Pesto-Operations.ps1:1111). The connection therefore stays in the elevated logon session.

2. When the code runs. This is exactly the target case of change 7. On an out-of-domain PC, or with an explicit credential, the token cannot read the marker. Get-PestoCoordinationRoot (Pesto-Policy.ps1:99-100) and every worker request carry `Credential=$script:cred`, which is the AD admin account set at Pesto-Authentication.ps1:68.
   - Case (a) holds. After Pesto closes (cancel, failed join, or no reboot), any elevated process in that Windows session reaches the registry server, and its other shares through the same SMB session, as the technician's AD account.

3. Case (b) holds, but only across processes.
   - Login happens once, at startup (Pesto-Core.ps1:4970-4975), so there is no credential switch inside one process.
   - A second Pesto started in the same logon session under another account sees `[IO.Directory]::Exists($share)` as true. That check is at Pesto-Policy.ps1:85 and Pesto-Names.ps1:229. It reuses the first account's connection without checking whose it is.
   - So registry and lock writes run under the first identity while the receipts name the second. If the first account can read but not write, the second technician's writes fail until logoff, even though that account has the rights.

4. Weak cases.
   - (c) needs a leftover connection that cannot read the share, which the reuse check makes unlikely.
   - (d) is unlikely with one technician, because Add-Computer uses the same `$CRED` (Pesto-Operations.ps1:1120) as the connection, and the same credential does not trigger 1219. It only applies after an earlier connection by a different account to the DC used for the join.

The defect is real. Severity is medium at most: credential residue plus wrong-identity reuse.
verdict.adjusted_fix:
- Workers must not open connections. Make at most one connection, from the main runspace, and record that Pesto created it (share, and the account used).
- In $Win.Add_Closed, after the reservation release in Stop-PestoSharedNameTimer, cancel the connection, but only when Pesto created it. Use WNetCancelConnection2(share, 0, $false) through Add-Type, or `net use \\srv\share /delete /y`; Remove-PSDrive only works in the runspace that holds the drive. Never cancel a connection the user made.
- In workers, if the share is not reachable, return a clear "partage inaccessible" error and let the main runspace connect.
- Before reusing an existing connection to the share server, check that its user matches $script:cred.UserName, for example Win32_NetworkConnection.UserName or the output of `net use`. If it differs, stop with an explicit message that suggests deleting the connection. Map error 1219 to the same message.
- Correct the comments at Pesto-Policy.ps1:79 and Pesto-Names.ps1:225: the connection lasts for the logon session until it is cancelled or the user logs off.

confirmed.title: Close-time release misses a reservation whose New-ADComputer is still in flight, leaving an orphaned 'Réservé par Pesto' account
confirmed.scenario: Start-PestoJoinADReservation (line 868) runs 'JoinADReserve' as an ordinary async op. $script:JoinADReservation is only set later, in its success callback (line 891). 'JoinADReserve' is not in the mutation list, so Add_Closing does not block the close. If the technician closes Pesto while the screen still shows 'Réservation du nom dans l'AD' (AD module import plus New-ADComputer can take several seconds from an out-of-domain station), Stop-PestoJoinADReservationAtClose sees no reservation and returns. Add_Closed then sends BeginStop to the op, but New-ADComputer may already have committed. The callback never runs, so the account stays in AD with the 'Réservé par Pesto' description and blocks that number for every station. Change 4 was meant to prevent exactly this.
confirmed.fix: Record the pending reservation (name, OU, DC) in a script variable before starting JoinADReserve. At close, if JoinADReserve is still running, wait for it within the same 8 s budget, or look up the account by sAMAccountName plus the Pesto description and this station or user, and release it under the same 'never used' checks. Alternatively, have Add_Closing wait for or refuse the close while JoinADReserve is running.

verdict.evidence:
I tried to refute this and could not. Every step of the scenario holds in the current code.

1. **The reservation is only recorded by the callback.** `Start-PestoJoinADReservation` (Pesto-Join.ps1:861-872) starts the 'JoinADReserve' async op. `$script:JoinADReservation` is set only in `Complete-PestoJoinADReservation` (Pesto-Join.ps1:891), and that runs on a dispatcher tick (90 ms, Pesto-Async.ps1:224) after the worker has finished New-ADComputer and then Get-ADComputer (Pesto-Join.ps1:849-857). Nothing records a pending reservation before the op starts.

2. **Closing is not blocked during the reservation.** `Add_Closing` (Pesto-Core.ps1:5200-5210) cancels the close only when `$script:Running` is set or `Test-PestoQueueWorkerStillActive` finds an active op. That check only covers QueueAction, DomainJoin, DirectAction and RecoveryAction (Pesto-Async.ps1:80); JoinADReserve is not among them. `Set-PestoJoinBusy` (Pesto-Join.ps1:341-347) only disables the form fields and tabs, not the window close. The reservation runs before the modal `Confirm-YesNo`, so the window can be closed.

3. **The close-time release returns early.** In `Add_Closed`, `Stop-PestoJoinADReservationAtClose` runs first (Pesto-Core.ps1:5185). It returns at once because `$script:JoinADReservation` is still null (Pesto-Join.ps1:918-919).

4. **The window is wider than the finding says.** The worker is not stopped right away. `Add_Closed` first calls `Stop-PestoSharedNameTimer`, which waits up to 3 s synchronously (Pesto-Names.ps1, `WaitOne(3000)`). Only after that does the loop call `Stop-PestoAsyncOperation 'JoinADReserve'`. So a close during the AD module import can still let New-ADComputer go through.

5. **Nothing clears the account afterwards.** `Stop-PestoAsyncOperation` removes the op and calls `BeginStop`, or does nothing if the worker already finished. Either way the callback is ignored (Pesto-Async.ps1:107-122). Then `Quit 0` calls `exit` (Pesto-Core.ps1:5272, 1218). Once New-ADComputer has reached the DC, the account stays with the "Réservé par Pesto ..." description.

6. **Nothing reclaims it later.** `ReservedByPesto` comes only from the in-memory `$script:JoinADReservation` (Pesto-Join.ps1:317-319), so a later Pesto run does not recognise the account. The name check treats it as taken, which blocks that number for every station.

This gap is narrower than a regression, since before the diff nothing was released at close. Still, change 4's stated goal of not leaving an unused Pesto-reserved account is not met when Pesto is closed while the screen shows 'Réservation du nom dans l'AD'. Severity: low.
verdict.adjusted_fix:
In `Stop-PestoJoinADReservationAtClose`, handle an in-flight reservation before the `if(-not $r){return}` early exit:

- If `Test-PestoAsyncOperationRunning 'JoinADReserve'` is true, take `$op=$script:PestoAsyncOperations['JoinADReserve']`.
- Wait on `$op.Async.AsyncWaitHandle` for whatever remains of the 8 s budget. This also covers a worker that has finished but whose callback has not run yet.
- Call `EndInvoke` on `$op.PowerShell` and take the last output.
- If its `State` is 'Reserved' and it has a `Guid`, build the release request from `Name`, `Guid` and the DC taken from the plan in the op's callback context. Release it with the same worker, so the same "never used" checks apply (name, description, DNSHostName, SPN).
- Remove the op from `$script:PestoAsyncOperations` so the later `Stop-PestoAsyncOperation` loop ignores it.
- If the timeout expires, log a WARN naming the account that may be left behind.

Simpler alternative: in `Add_Closing`, refuse the close with a short message while `Test-PestoAsyncOperationRunning 'JoinADReserve'` is true; the reservation is bounded by a 60 s timeout.

In either case, also send `BeginStop` to JoinADReserve before the 3 s `Stop-PestoSharedNameTimer` wait, not after it, so a close during the module import does not give New-ADComputer extra time to run.

confirmed.title: The registry-held switch reuses the AD-taken path: false 'déjà utilisé dans l'AD' Journal line and the name is banned for the whole session
confirmed.scenario: Technicians A and B both start on P..0001. A's registry reservation reaches B during B's check. Complete-PestoJoinCheck (Join.ps1:584-585) or Complete-PestoDirectPreflight (Direct.ps1:310-311) then calls Select-PestoJoinNextName / Select-PestoDirectNextName. Both functions write to the Journal 'JONCTION : P..0001 déjà utilisé dans l'AD ; nom suivant proposé…' (Join.ps1:477) or 'RENOMMAGE : … déjà utilisé dans l'AD' (Direct.ps1:262). That is false: the name is only held in the registry for 15 minutes. Both functions also add the name to $script:PestoTakenNames (Join.ps1:469, Direct.ps1:249), a set that is only reset when Pesto restarts. If A cancels or the hold expires, B's Pesto never offers P..0001 again, and the lowest numbers stay as gaps for that technician. The same happens when the 'Held' is a false positive about our own file. The Reserve worker reports Held with 'autre poste (réservation en cours d'écriture)' whenever its exclusive open fails because any snapshot reader has the file open (Names.ps1:303-304). The check then switches away from, and bans, the technician's own reserved name. Also, the success path resets JoinAutoNext/DirectAutoNext before the held test (Join.ps1:577, Direct.ps1:295), so the 5-switch cap never applies to held switches.
confirmed.fix: Add a registry-specific variant, or a -Temporary switch, to Select-*NextName that does not add the name to PestoTakenNames and logs 'réservé par <holder> dans le registre partagé' instead of 'déjà utilisé dans l'AD'. The dynamic exclusion through Test-PestoNameReservedByOther already keeps held names out of the lists. Optionally, keep counting held switches against the cap.

verdict.evidence:
I tried to refute this by tracing the code. The main claims hold, but two side claims carry little weight.

1. **The Journal and audit lines are false (confirmed).** The diff adds a call to the AD-taken helpers at two places: DEV/wad/Pesto-Join.ps1:584-585 and DEV/wad/Pesto-Direct.ps1:310-311. Both helpers write a fixed log line that ignores -Reason: Join.ps1:477 writes "JONCTION : $TakenName déjà utilisé dans l'AD ; nom suivant proposé" and Direct.ps1:262 writes "RENOMMAGE : … déjà utilisé dans l'AD". Add-LogLine (Pesto-Journal.ps1:139-149) also calls Write-AuditLine, so the false statement ends up in the on-disk audit trail. The AD check has just passed at that point (Join.ps1:577-578 shows 'Vérifications préalables réussies').
   - The same scenario also produces a contradiction. The Held reply arrives while JoinBusy or DirectBusy is true, so Complete-PestoSharedNameOperation (Pesto-Names.ps1, the new busy branch) has already logged "NOMS : X aussi réservé par Y pendant votre opération ; le nom reste revérifié dans l'AD avant l'écriture", which says the operation continues on that name. The next line then says it is used in AD and was switched.
   - The UI title 'Nom déjà pris' is also shown (Join.ps1:476). In the default mode (RandomNameChoice < 2), the UI message also says the new name is the 'premier numéro libre de la série dans l'AD'.

2. **The name is banned for the whole session (confirmed).** Select-PestoJoinNextName (Join.ps1:469) and Select-PestoDirectNextName (Direct.ps1:249) add TakenName to $script:PestoTakenNames. That set is reset only in Initialize-PestoJoinUI (Join.ps1:768), which runs once because it returns early when JoinUI already exists. Get-PestoJoinNameCandidates (Join.ps1:442) and Update-NameList (Pesto-Core.ps1:3109) skip those names permanently.
   - This contradicts the intent stated at Join.ps1:443: a name held in the registry is excluded only "tant que la réservation court", through Test-PestoNameReservedByOther.
   - The effect: if the other station abandons the name (picks another name or closes Pesto), this station never offers it again. This matters most in Direct mode, where one session renames many PCs. The 'premier numéro libre' text then becomes wrong too.

3. **A false Held about our own file is possible but rare (plausible).** The Reserve worker returns Held with Holder 'autre poste (réservation en cours d'écriture)' and HolderExpiresUtc='' when the FileShare.None open fails (Pesto-Names.ps1:303-304). Snapshot reads use ReadAllText, which opens the file with FileShare.Read, so a read in progress makes that open fail. Complete-PestoSharedNameOperation then stores the name in SharedNameOthers with ExpiresUtc ''. Test-PestoNameReservedByOther (Names.ps1:349-357) returns $true when the date cannot be parsed.
   - During a check, the busy tick re-reserves our own name only on a half-TTL renewal, or after an earlier Reserve timed out. So the case needs a renewal during the check plus a snapshot read at the same moment, which is unlikely.
   - The worker behaviour already existed. What is new is the consequence: before this diff, a false Held only hid the name until the next snapshot (≤30 s). Now it can switch away from the station's own reserved name and ban it.

4. **The 5-switch cap does not apply to held switches (true in code, harmless).** The counter is reset at Join.ps1:577 and Direct.ps1:295, before the held test. In practice the loop is bounded: each switch needs a real Held reply from another station, and the lists already skip names known to be held.

Overall the defect is real, but low-to-medium severity: misleading audit text and numbering gaps for the current session. There is no AD-integrity impact, because AD re-checks the name and the technician confirms before any write.
verdict.adjusted_fix:
Add a switch such as -RegistryHeld to Select-PestoJoinNextName and Select-PestoDirectNextName and pass it from Pesto-Join.ps1:585 and Pesto-Direct.ps1:311.

With the switch set:
- Do not add TakenName to $script:PestoTakenNames. The dynamic exclusion through Test-PestoNameReservedByOther already keeps the name out of the lists while the reservation is active, and lets it come back once it expires or a snapshot clears it. A false Held about our own file then clears itself within 30 s.
- Log using the reason, for example "JONCTION : $TakenName $Reason Nom suivant proposé : $next." (and the same with "RENOMMAGE" for Direct), instead of the hard-coded "déjà utilisé dans l'AD".
- Use a title such as 'Nom réservé par un autre poste : nom suivant proposé'.

Also reword the busy-Held Journal line in Complete-PestoSharedNameOperation, because the operation no longer simply "continues" on that name once the check succeeds. Something like "… ; un autre nom sera proposé à la fin du contrôle" fits.

Optionally, move the JoinAutoNext/DirectAutoNext reset (Join.ps1:577, Direct.ps1:295) after the held test so held switches count toward the 5-switch cap.

confirmed.title: An AD reservation still being created at close is orphaned; the new close cleanup cannot see it
confirmed.scenario: Start-PestoJoinADReservation shows 'Réservation du nom dans l'AD' while the JoinADReserve worker runs New-ADComputer (1-3 s out of domain). The Closing handler does not block on JoinADReserve: it is not one of the names in Test-PestoQueueWorkerStillActive (Pesto-Async.ps1:80), and Closing stops only JoinCheck/JoinStatus. If the technician closes during that window, $script:JoinADReservation is still $null, because it is set only in the completion callback (Join.ps1:891), so Stop-PestoJoinADReservationAtClose returns immediately. The Add_Closed loop then only BeginStops the worker, which often has already created the account. A 'Réservé par Pesto' computer account stays in the OU and blocks that number for every station, which is the case diff item 4 was meant to prevent.
confirmed.fix: In Add_Closing, either cancel the close or wait briefly while 'JoinADReserve' is running. Or, at close, wait for the in-flight JoinADReserve op and release the GUID it returns.

verdict.evidence:
I could not refute it. Every step of the scenario holds in the code.
- Start-PestoJoinADReservation (Pesto-Join.ps1:861-872) starts the async op 'JoinADReserve'. Its worker runs New-ADComputer and then Get-ADComputer (Pesto-Join.ps1:847-855).
- $script:JoinADReservation is set only in the OnSuccess callback Complete-PestoJoinADReservation (Pesto-Join.ps1:891). That callback runs on the dispatcher timer after the op completes.
- Nothing stops the close during this window. Add_Closing (Pesto-Core.ps1:5199-5209) cancels only for $script:Running or Test-PestoQueueWorkerStillActive. That function matches only QueueAction, DomainJoin, DirectAction and RecoveryAction (Pesto-Async.ps1:78-83). $script:JoinBusy is not checked. Add_Closing stops only JoinCheck and JoinStatus.
- In Add_Closed, Stop-PestoJoinADReservationAtClose runs first (Pesto-Core.ps1:5185). It reads $script:JoinADReservation, which is still $null, and returns (Pesto-Join.ps1:918-919).
- The loop at Pesto-Core.ps1:5197 then calls Stop-PestoAsyncOperation 'JoinADReserve'. That only removes the op and calls BeginStop (Pesto-Async.ps1:109-121), so the callback is dropped. BeginStop does not reliably stop a New-ADComputer call that is already in flight, and the account is often created already.
- A second path has the same result: the worker has already returned, but the timer has not yet run the callback when the user closes. The guard is $null and the GUID is lost.
Outcome: a computer account described as 'Réservé par Pesto…' stays in the OU, and the name is taken for every station. Diff item 4 exists to prevent exactly this.
Limits:
- This is a gap in the new cleanup, not a regression. Before the diff, every reservation was left at close.
- The window is short: the 1-3 s New-ADComputer round trip plus at most one timer tick. Severity low is appropriate.
verdict.adjusted_fix:
Either option below fixes it; option 1 keeps the window open and is the more robust one.

1. Harvest the result in Stop-PestoJoinADReservationAtClose. Before reading $script:JoinADReservation:
   - If Test-PestoAsyncOperationRunning 'JoinADReserve', take $op=$script:PestoAsyncOperations['JoinADReserve'].
   - Wait on $op.Async.AsyncWaitHandle.WaitOne(N). N is the reserve budget, taken out of the existing 8 s total.
   - If the wait completes, call $op.PowerShell.EndInvoke($op.Async). If the result has State 'Reserved' and a Guid, build $r from Name, Guid and DC, taking DC from the request or plan.
   - Then run the existing synchronous Release on that $r.
   - Remove the op from $script:PestoAsyncOperations so the loop at Core:5197 does not BeginStop it.
   - If the wait times out, log a WARN that names the account, because it may have been created.
   This also covers the case where the op has completed but its callback has not yet been dispatched.

2. Block the close instead. In Add_Closing, if Test-PestoAsyncOperationRunning 'JoinADReserve', set $e.Cancel=$true and show "Réservation du nom dans l'AD en cours, réessayez dans quelques secondes". The worker's TimeoutSec is 60, so the block is bounded.

rejected.title: When no other name is available, the new registry branch carries on with the held name after the name list has already changed
rejected.why:
The fall-through after `Select-*NextName` returns `$false` is in the code, but the finding's trigger cannot occur in realistic use.

1. **The five-switch cap cannot fire in these branches.** `Select-PestoJoinNextName` returns `$false` early only when `JoinAutoNext > 5` (Pesto-Join.ps1:471). The counter is reset just before the new branch: `$script:JoinAutoNext=0` at Pesto-Join.ps1:577, ahead of the branch at 584-585. The Direct side does the same with `$script:DirectAutoNext=0` at Pesto-Direct.ps1:295, ahead of the branch at 310-313. When `Select-*` runs from the new branches, the counter becomes 1, so that early return never fires.

2. **The other early returns are excluded by the branch conditions.**
   - `-not $TakenName` cannot happen: the plan passed `Get-PestoJoinPlanErrors`, so a valid name is present.
   - `Existing.IsChecked` cannot happen: the branch requires `-not AllowExisting`, and the plan key compared at line 560 includes `AllowExisting`.

3. **The only remaining `$false` is an empty list, which means the whole series is used up.** The list comes from `Get-AvailableMachines` (Pesto-Core.ps1:1513-1516), which returns every free number from 001 to 999 in the series. Both list rebuilds remove only:
   - names in `PestoTakenNames`, which is filled with `SeriesTaken`, the names actually found in AD (Pesto-Join.ps1:187, Pesto-Core.ps1:722);
   - names reserved by other stations in the registry, usually a handful.

   Both `Update-PestoJoinNames` (Pesto-Join.ps1:503-504) and `Update-NameList` (Pesto-Core.ps1:3109-3111) select an item whenever the list has one. So `$next` is empty only when every number from 001 to 999 except X is in AD, already found taken, or reserved by another station. The finding's "series nearly exhausted" is not enough; the series must be completely exhausted.

4. **Even then, the AD outcome is the same as before the diff.** Before the diff, this path went straight to `Start-PestoJoinADReservation` or the confirmation with X, with no registry check. AD still decides: creating the account is atomic, and the other station gets `Taken` and moves to its next name (Pesto-Join.ps1:883-886). What changes is only in the interface: the list is empty and the automatic re-check stops at "Formulaire incomplet". `Test-PestoJoinADReservationStale` then removes the leftover reservation of X (Pesto-Join.ps1:939-945). This only happens with a fully exhausted series, where the tool already shows "Aucun nom disponible".

This is not a defect with a plausible failure scenario.

rejected.title: Close-time AD release deletes the reserved account even after an uncertain join (97/98)
rejected.why:
The finding is right that the code contradicts its own comment, but the harmful outcome it describes (deleting an account the machine is bound to) cannot happen on these code paths.

1. **The account is kept after 97/98, and close does release it.** `Complete-PestoJoinExecution` keeps `$script:JoinADReservation` on 97/98 (Pesto-Join.ps1:643-646). `Stop-PestoJoinADReservationAtClose` (Pesto-Join.ps1:914-937) releases it without checking `JoinLocked`. That part is accurate.

2. **Close cannot race a running join.** `Add_Closing` (Pesto-Core.ps1:5199-5205) cancels the close while `Test-PestoQueueWorkerStillActive` is true. That function (Pesto-Async.ps1:78-83) covers `DomainJoin` until its runspace `Async.IsCompleted`, even after a monitor timeout. So the release always runs after `Add-Computer` has returned or thrown.

3. **The release refuses any account that was used.** The Release worker (Pesto-Join.ps1:836-841) keeps the account (`Kept`) when it has a `DNSHostName` or any SPN. It reads from `r.DC`, the same DC that `Add-Computer -Server $dcFqdn` used (plan DC, enforced by `New-PestoJoinPlanFromUI` line 318).

4. **The "password set but no dNSHostName/SPN yet" state does not arise.** On Windows 10/11, NetJoinDomain reuses a precreated account through `NetpModifyComputerObjectInDs`. That is one `ldap_modify` writing `unicodePwd`, `DnsHostName`, `ServicePrincipalName` and `userAccountControl` together.
   - If that write fails, the join fails and rolls back, so the machine is not joined.
   - If NetJoinDomain returns an error later (local LSA step, RPC 1722, 1219 at connect), the local join is rolled back. The machine is never bound to the account. Deleting an unused, unbound "Réservé par Pesto" account breaks no trust.

5. **Every 97 where the join did succeed leaves the attributes in place.** These cases are:
   - the monitor timeout/cancel override (Pesto-Join.ps1:245);
   - the receipt-write failure (Pesto-Join.ps1:251);
   - `Test-PestoConfirmedChange` returning false (Pesto-Operations.ps1:1135);
   - PS 5.1 `Add-Computer` throwing on the local rename after a successful JoinWithNewName.

   In each, the DS already holds `dNSHostName`/SPN from the join, so the release returns `Kept`.

6. **The only theoretical gap is too narrow to count.** It needs the downlevel SAM fallback, plus a failed `dNSHostName`/SPN LDAP write that does not stop the join, plus a separate 97 trigger. That fallback needs LDAP broken while ADWS still works and the creator lacks write rights on its own object. This is not the reviewer's scenario.

7. **The lack of a receipt or lock is not new.** `Stop-PestoJoinADReservation` already releases the same way, and `Test-PestoJoinADReservationStale` (Pesto-Join.ps1:939-945, run every second by the pulse at line 707) already calls it after 97/98 once the form changes.

What remains is a mismatch with the documented intent ("un résultat incertain le garde"), not a concrete failure.

rejected.title: Closing Pesto deletes the AD account Pesto reserved even after an uncertain join (97/98 or execution error), which the existing design deliberately keeps
rejected.why:
The code path the reviewer describes exists, but it cannot do the harm they claim.

What is true:
- Complete-PestoJoinExecution keeps $script:JoinADReservation on 97/98 (DEV/wad/Pesto-Join.ps1:643-646).
- Complete-PestoJoinExecutionError never clears it.
- The new Add_Closed hook (DEV/wad/Pesto-Core.ps1:5185) calls Stop-PestoJoinADReservationAtClose (DEV/wad/Pesto-Join.ps1:914-937). That function does not check JoinLocked or the receipt phase.

Why the failure cannot happen:
1. The function only runs the Release worker, which deletes nothing unless the account is unused. Get-ADComputer runs against $Request.DC and the worker returns Kept (no Remove-ADComputer) if DNSHostName is non-empty, any ServicePrincipalName exists, or the name or the "Réservé par Pesto" description changed (Pesto-Join.ps1:833-840).
2. The read happens on the same DC that did the join. $r.DC is plan.DC (Pesto-Join.ps1:891), and AddToDomain calls Add-Computer -Server $dcFqdn built from that same $plan.DC (Pesto-Operations.ps1:1086, 1138). There is no replication gap.
3. AddToDomain calls Add-Computer -NewName with no -Options (Pesto-Operations.ps1:1124-1133). Its documented default is AccountCreate plus JoinWithNewName, not DeferSPNSet. When NetJoinDomain reuses an existing account, it writes userAccountControl, DnsHostName, ServicePrincipalName and unicodePwd in one LDAP modify on that DC (NetpModifyComputerObjectInDs). Before that write the PC cannot hold the account's secret, and the local domain membership is set only afterwards. A failed write rolls the join back, so the PC is not bound.
4. So the reviewer's case "PC bound to the account while DNSHostName and SPN are empty" does not occur with this call. The same holds for:
   - 97 from a timeout or late success: the join finished, so DNSHostName is set and the account is Kept.
   - 97 from a receipt-write failure after code 10: same.
   - A Windows refusal: the account was never used, so deleting it is correct.
5. Close cannot overlap an Add-Computer that is still running. Add_Closing cancels the close while Test-PestoQueueWorkerStillActive sees DomainJoin not completed (Pesto-Core.ps1:5201, Pesto-Async.ps1:78-83). The timer operation stays registered after a timeout until the worker really ends (Pesto-Async.ps1:271-296, 319).
6. Deleting an unused account does not change how an Uncertain receipt is verified. Get-PestoJoinObservationDecision stops at "Windows ne confirme pas encore le domaine attendu" for a PC outside the domain, before it ever looks at the AD object (DEV/wad/Pesto-JoinRecovery.ps1:92-93).
7. The existing Stop-PestoJoinADReservation and Test-PestoJoinADReservationStale paths already rely on this same DNSHostName/SPN guard.

What remains is only a design inconsistency. The comments at Pesto-Join.ps1:642 and 819-820 say an uncertain result "garde" the account, while the close path relies on the "never used" guard instead. That is not a concrete defect.

rejected.title: Synchronous close-time waits (up to 8 s + 3 s, plus runspace and AD-module start-up) hold the session mutex after the window has gone, so an immediate relaunch is refused
rejected.why:
The headline claim, a refused relaunch "at nearly every close" when a CoordinationRoot is set, does not hold. The code allows only a narrow degraded case.

1) Normal close cost. Stop-PestoSharedNameTimer (Pesto-Names.ps1:534-551) runs a Release-mode worker. That worker (Pesto-Names.ps1:217-...) does only local regex work, one `[IO.Directory]::Exists`, a read of the marker and file deletes. With a reachable share this is a fresh runspace plus a few SMB operations, well under 1 s. The 3 s limit is reached only when the share is slow or unreachable. Get-PestoSharedNameSettings (Names.ps1:342-347) reads only local settings, so the UI thread does no unbounded UNC I/O before that limit.

2) The AD release is rare and fully bounded. Stop-PestoJoinADReservationAtClose (Pesto-Join.ps1:914-938) returns at once unless `$script:JoinADReservation` exists. That needs ReserveNamesInAD and a checked but unused reservation; an ordinary displayed name does not create one. The finding says module import is not counted in the limit. That is wrong: the AD import runs inside the worker started by `BeginInvoke`, so `WaitOne(8000)` covers it. Only `[PowerShell]::Create()` and opening the runspace fall outside it, a fraction of a second in a process that already has runspaces running.

3) A relaunch takes several seconds to reach the mutex. In Pesto-Startup.ps1, the check at 479-481 comes after these steps:
- PowerShell 5.1 starts.
- Test-PestoPackage hashes every runtime file, including the 1.1 MB DLL (Startup.ps1:387).
- Test-PestoRuntimeReady (Integrity.ps1:134-171) runs the real parser over about 1 MB of .ps1 source, then calls `Add-Type -Path Pesto-LogWriter.cs`, which compiles through csc.exe.
- On the usual non-elevated launch, the route is 'Elevate' (Startup.ps1:36-42, 447-453). The user then answers the UAC prompt, and the elevated relay repeats all of the above plus Import-PestoStartupState before reaching the mutex.

Pesto has no automatic self-relaunch. A grep for Start-Process or relancer finds only messages telling the user to relaunch Pesto.exe by hand. So in the normal case the old process frees `Global\GP_Session_*` (finally block at Startup.ps1:496-497, which runs on `exit`) long before a new launch checks it.

4) What remains. The refusal can occur only when both close-time releases hit their limits, an unused AD reservation also exists, and the technician relaunches an already-elevated Pesto within roughly 4-8 s. That means about 8 s for the AD release, 3 s for the registry release and up to 3 s for the existing Stop-PestoAuditWriter `Close(3000)`. Even then the message is transient and a second try succeeds. That is a degraded-network edge case, not the regression described for almost every close.
